headline: GHRP-2
punch: More potent than ipamorelin. That cuts both ways.

headline: What it actually is
body: A synthetic hexapeptide agonist at **GHS-R1a**, the ghrelin receptor, signalling through Gq and PLC at the pituitary. Same receptor as ipamorelin, different selectivity profile. | It also acts at the hypothalamic level, where ghrelin signalling opposes somatostatin's inhibitory effect on GHRH neurons. So it works at two sites rather than one, which is part of why it is more potent.
punch: Two sites of action. More potency, less selectivity.

headline: It is measurably stronger
body: At **300 mcg** fasted, GHRP-2 produces roughly **5 to 7 ng/mL** peak serum GH. Add **300 mcg** of CJC-1295 no-DAC at the same time and peak GH rises to roughly **15 to 20 ng/mL**. | That is the synergy made concrete. The two pathways are separate, so combining them roughly triples the peak rather than adding to it.

headline: The 30-day human data
body: Bowers ran GHRP-2 as a continuous 30-day subcutaneous infusion in healthy older men and women and measured at day 1, 14 and 30. | On day 1 it drove pulsatile GH secretion by **more than 3 fold**, P < 0.001. By day 14 and day 30 it was still driving it by **more than 1.8 fold**. The paper's own summary is that 30 days **sustains a physiologically activated somatotropic axis**.
punch: It fades. It does not stop.

headline: It fades about 40%
body: Read the same numbers the other way. Three-fold on day one, 1.8-fold two weeks later, with nothing changed except time. That is roughly a 40 percent loss of effect while you keep paying full price. | And the receptor data explains it: **24 hours of continuous GHRP infusion attenuated the bolus response** while 14 days of continuous GHRH did not. GHS-R1a is the rate-limiting receptor.
punch: ==3 fold on day 1. 1.8 fold by day 14.==

headline: Cortisol and prolactin
body: This is where it separates from ipamorelin. GHRP-2 drives **cortisol and prolactin** elevation through direct pituitary corticotroph stimulation. Ipamorelin is the only one in the class that does not. | And it desensitises faster: the ranking is hexarelin > GHRP-2 > GHRP-6 ≈ ipamorelin. So you are buying potency with both an adrenal liability and quicker fatigue.
punch: Potency bought with cortisol and faster fade.

headline: Cortisol works against you
body: The problem compounds. **Glucocorticoids blunt GHRP efficacy**, along with glucose, free fatty acids and exogenous GH, because they all raise somatostatin tone. | So a compound that raises cortisol is raising one of the inputs that gates its own effect. That loop does not exist with ipamorelin, and it is the strongest argument for the cleaner compound.
punch: _It raises a hormone that gates its own effect._

headline: Switch or alternate
body: The cleanest mitigation is compound choice rather than dosing. Ipamorelin reaches the same receptor with no cortisol or prolactin liability and the slowest desensitisation in the class. | If the potency is the point, the asymmetry gives you the other move: the GHRH arm does not fatigue over 14 days, so that is the component to keep constant and this is the one to rest.
punch: Rest the GHRP. Keep the GHRH arm.

headline: Space, do not stack
body: There is a published diagnostic for which problem you have. If a second same-day pulse is blunted **even when you rotate to a GHRH analogue**, which has no GHS-R1a to desensitise, then the blunting is feedback rather than receptor downregulation. | That distinction tells you whether spacing fixes it or whether you are fighting somatostatin and IGF-1 feedback, which spacing will not fix.
punch: There is a test for which problem you have.

headline: No height endpoint
body: The human data here is GH secretion over 30 days in healthy older adults. That is real human data and it is better than most compounds on this list have. | It is not a height trial, a bone trial, or any clinical endpoint. And the class ceiling applies: secretagogues work within a roughly physiological envelope, do not exceed exogenous GH on linear growth, and cannot reopen a fused plate.
punch: Good secretion data. No outcome data.

headline: Verdict
body: More potent than ipamorelin and better documented in humans over 30 days, with a clear synergy number when paired with a GHRH analogue. | It costs you cortisol and prolactin, it fades faster, and the cortisol it raises feeds back into the gate that limits it. For most purposes the cleaner compound at a slightly lower peak is the better trade.
punch: Stronger, dirtier, and it undermines itself.
